newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIRS sees EU 97/98 beet sugar output at 15.99 mln.
newsitem.headline: FIRS sees EU 97/98 beet sugar output at 15.99 mln.

text.p: French sugar intervention board FIRS predicted on Tuesday that 1997/98 sugar beet production in the European Union may decline to 15.987 million tonnes from 16.515 million in 1996/97.
In its first forecast for the new 1997/98 season, FIRS also predicted France may produce 4.20 million tonnes of beet sugar against 4.226 million in 1996/97.

In its monthly report for April, FIRS said the forecast for the European Union was based on sowings data provided by member states at the April 9 sugar management committee meeting and on average sugar yields for the past five campaigns.
The forecast for EU 1997/98 sugar yields was down to 7.84 tonnes per hectare from 8.17 tonnes in 1996/97.
EU sowings were put at 2.040 million hectares, up from 2.021 million in 1996/97.
The output estimate for France assumed sowings would slightly ease to 420,000 hectares from 422,000 hectares and sugar yield reach 10.0 tonnes per hectare from 10.01 tonnes in 1996/97.
FIRS said that as of mid-April there were worries about the possible impact of drought on crops, but the estimate for France did not reflect the weather element at this stage.
"We think that for the moment there is no reason to include this element in our estimate," FIRS said.
It said that despite a prolonged dry spell during the previous campaign, the French sugar yield came close to record levels.
Last week beet planters said they were worried that prolonged cold and dry conditions might cancel the benefits of early sowings.
